paragraphs: For people suited to exploring this occupation first: willing to verify equipment, operating conditions, exposure, and accident records and to write reviewable hazard control recommendations. Under the U.S. occupational definition, specialists lean toward assessment and programs, while technicians lean toward sampling, inspection, and implementation.

Judging fit means seeing whether you can distinguish observed facts, instrument readings, regulatory requirements, and conclusions still to be verified; calibration, time, place, and responsible person stay in the record.

Use the fully fictional A guard, B cleaning agent, and C wet-floor records for a 60-minute paper exercise: log facts and unknowns and write control candidates and escalation targets. Do not touch real equipment or chemicals.

Deliver a three-line hazard register, a missing-evidence list, and a review column. Reflect on whether you can acknowledge unknowns, explain the hierarchy of controls, and hand over to an authorized person, rather than issuing a release conclusion from a single reading.

This page covers the shared field of U.S. O*NET 19-5011.00 safety and health specialists and 19-5012.00 safety and health technicians; the two are listed separately for education, tasks, and wages, and Chinese posts are verified against actual recruitment and qualification rules.

entries: Focus of the work: occupational health and safety specialists and technicians turn workplace observations, exposure data, and accident records into hazard judgments, control programs, and corrective verification; specialists lean toward assessment design and technicians toward sampling implementation.
Inspectable output: identifying chemical, physical, biological, and ergonomic hazards.
Complete workflow: proposing and implementing control programs according to the hierarchy of controls.

paragraphs: The work object is the environment workers are in, equipment guarding, chemical or physical exposure, and accident and corrective records; outputs include hazard assessments, sampling records, control programs, or review evidence.

Some posts require entering factories, construction sites, or other hazardous locations, and there is also report analysis and training work. Work arrangements depend on the employer and industry, and fixed hours cannot be presumed from the occupational title.

Common materials include SDSs, checklists, instrument calibration and sampling chains, accident records, original regulatory texts, and corrective ledgers; any software output should be traceable to the original record.

When collaborating with frontline workers, supervisors, engineering, medical, or regulatory roles, state facts and unknowns first, then write the responsible person, deadline, and abnormality escalation path.
Quality is not decided by report length; it depends on whether hazards were identified, whether controls were implemented, whether retesting supports the conclusion, and whether open items are clear.

Specialists who design and assess do not automatically hold the authority to stop or restart equipment, and technicians who carry out sampling are not thereby able to sign compliance conclusions independently. Authority follows the jurisdiction and employer procedures.

When choosing an adjacent direction, look first at the protected object and the delivery: this occupation faces worker exposure and operational control; environmental posts face environmental media, engineering posts lean toward system design, and ergonomics posts lean toward human-machine tasks. Shared inspection ability does not automatically transfer qualification or authorization.

The basis for comparison is the tasks of the two O*NET safety and health occupations, the BLS occupational descriptions, and the work objects of each direction; these U.S. task definitions cannot replace Chinese job postings or statutory authority.

Using the same fictional A/B/C case for comparison: would you rather check sampling and site records, design hazard controls, produce equipment engineering plans, or investigate environmental or ergonomic problems? Compare target object, method, and output.

Specialists assess multiple hazard types and design controls, while technicians lean more toward on-site inspection, collecting information, and assisting implementation; neither can approve a return to work on the strength of a job title alone.

If you like synthesizing evidence, proposing a hierarchy of controls, and reviewing effectiveness, start by exploring the specialist direction; if you prefer instruments and site records, compare technician posts.
People preparing to enter the field
First try checklist generation on the fictional A/B/C records, verifying the original facts and unknowns item by item.
Safety technician
Within the authorized scope, verify calibration, sampling location, and duration; without quality control information, no exposure conclusion may be given.
Safety specialist
Verify model suggestions against site conditions, the hierarchy of controls, and regulatory applicability, and record rejected suggestions.
Employer responsible person
Limit pilot data and authority and specify responsibility for reviewing false positives and negatives, escalation, exit, and sign-off.

Evidence insufficient: the national independent wage median for Chinese occupational health and safety specialists and technicians was not obtained. A further reference is the 2025 average wage of 155,491 yuan/year (pre-tax) for professional technical personnel in enterprises above a designated size, which serves only as a broad cross-industry post reference for the specialist professional technical work direction and does not represent the wage of technicians or of the combined occupation.

The reference comes from the total row for professional technical personnel in Table 6 of the National Bureau of Statistics 2025 urban unit wage public tables, published May 15, 2026. The population here is professional technical personnel in enterprises above a designated size, not all government agencies, public institutions, or freelancers; the professional technical category is determined by actual tasks.

Evidence insufficient: the same-measure annual wage, monthly wage, and percentile distributions for these two occupations in China were not obtained. 155,491 yuan/year is a broad post average, not an occupational median, a new-hire rate, or a hiring offer; it is not used to infer personal monthly salary, and U.S. wages are not converted into Chinese income.

Professional assessment, hazard analysis, and control programs are the task basis for the specialist on this page, so the broad professional technical post figure can be used as background; the technician's sampling assistance cannot be automatically grouped on that basis. Actual pay should still be verified by city, employer, pre- or post-tax, fixed wage, allowances, and variable components.

U.S. BLS reports occupational health and safety specialists 19-5011 and technicians 19-5012 separately. The May 2025 median annual wages are 90,150 USD and 61,560 USD respectively; the two cannot be combined into one personal offer.

The wage reference period is May 2025; the employment stock base period is 2025, and the growth and average annual openings projection period is 2025—2035. Wage and employment years must not be interchanged.

The wage tables are in USD/year, with a separate official USD/hour series; without an individual's actual paid hours, taxes, and contract conditions, personal monthly salary or take-home income is not inferred.

The BLS wage percentiles and employment figures correspond respectively to U.S. occupations 19-5011 and 19-5012; Chinese posts, project contracts, and personal experience are not within these statistical populations.

Specialists and technicians are different occupations. The combined occupation 2025 median annual wage of 83,740 USD is used only when the 19-5000 combined measure is explicitly labeled, and does not replace either component.

The U.S. national wage percentiles come from the 2025 BLS data presented by O*NET: specialists and technicians each have P10, P25, P50, P75, P90. Percentiles cannot be interpreted directly as novice or senior levels, nor do they guarantee personal income.

paragraphs: RIASEC only helps raise interest questions. Choosing this occupation also depends on the hazard register, sampling quality control, control review samples, and post training.
Evidence level: an interest scale is self-reflection, not proof of occupational competence, hiring, or on-site authorization.

The following are work scenario risk prompts. Stopping work, isolation, sampling, and return to work in real settings must comply with local regulations and employer authorization; a paper case cannot replace on-site procedures.

The key failures in this occupation are failure to escalate a failed safeguard, drawing conclusions despite missing sampling quality control, extrapolating from a single reading, and corrections that were never reviewed. Each card gives the trigger, consequence, and control.

The risk cards are based on O*NET specialist and technician tasks, the BLS work environment, and the OSHA hazard prevention and control guidance; A/B/C are fictional exercises and do not represent real accidents or statutory thresholds.
Those directly affected are workers around the equipment, maintenance personnel, and the safety team responsible for escalating risk.

If a missing guard with unknown interlock status is mistakenly released, it may cause mechanical injury and delay control; equipment and return-to-work conditions must be verified by an authorized person.

U.S. BLS lists specialists and technicians separately: specialists usually need a relevant bachelor's degree, while technicians usually need at least a high school diploma plus on-the-job training; Chinese qualifications and on-site authorization are verified separately against local rules and employer notices.

A fully fictional paper case: at a packaging workshop, A was found at 09:00 to have the conveyor guard missing, and no interlock test record was provided; for the B cleaning agent C1 two containers had no labels and no SDS, and the air sampling lacked calibration, duration, and location; C had two wet-floor incidents in the same passage within 30 days, with no cleaning responsibility or review time recorded. First list facts, unknowns, possible consequences, and escalation targets; do not enter the hazard area or test equipment yourself.
Fact register

Reference delivery: for A, mark the missing guard and unknown interlock, escalate per unit procedure, and isolate the affected steps; for B, request the SDS and a compliant sampling chain, and do not fabricate concentration or exceedance conclusions; for C, investigate the source of the wet floor and record temporary isolation, cleaning responsibility, and review. The portfolio contains a three-line hazard register, a missing-evidence list, control priorities, responsible deadlines, and a review evidence column.
Plan and answers

Seven-day paper experience: Day 1 read BLS/O*NET and write the division of work; Day 2 transcribe the A/B/C facts and unknowns; Day 3 build the hazard register; Day 4 write candidate measures according to the OSHA hierarchy of controls; Day 5 build the sampling quality control and review columns; Day 6 ask a peer to point out omissions; Day 7 revise the portfolio and choose whether to continue exploring the specialist, technician, or an adjacent direction. Keep one file each day.
Seven-day trial

When finished, keep the hazard register, original inputs, missing-evidence list, control drafts, and the revisions made after challenge; the portfolio cannot replace a certificate, hiring, or on-site signing authority.

United States

entries.answer: O*NET lists U.S. safety and health specialists as 19-5011.00: evaluating work environments, investigating incidents, and designing or recommending control programs; technicians 19-5012.00 assist with inspections, collecting information, and implementing safety measures. BLS also reports the two separately for wages, employment, and typical education entry. Chinese job titles may merge duties or assign them differently, so verify the job description, equipment training, and signing authority before applying.
entries.question: What do occupational health and safety specialists and technicians do separately?

entries.answer: Safety and health engineers usually lean more toward engineering design of equipment, systems, and processes; the specialist on this page leans more toward workplace hazard assessment and control planning, and the technician toward sampling, inspection, and implementation of measures. All three may take part in cross-team projects, and no one's authority to stop or restart work or sign compliance can be presumed from a job title. When comparing target posts, look at the project deliverables, engineering coursework, instrument training, and employer authorization.
entries.question: How is the work divided among safety and health specialists, technicians, and engineers?

entries.answer: You can use the fully fictional A missing guard, B cleaning agent with no label and sampling quality control, and C wet-floor record as paper work samples. First list the knowns, unknowns, and potential consequences item by item, then write candidate measures, responsible persons, and review evidence according to the OSHA hierarchy of controls. For B, do not fill in a fictional concentration; for A, do not test the interlock yourself or approve a return to work. Deliver the hazard register, missing-evidence list, control draft, and reflection.
entries.question: What kind of work sample is suitable for testing your interest?

entries.answer: Sensors and AI can help aggregate inspection and sampling records, flag anomalies, or draft control options, and the ILO has also discussed the opportunities and risks of digital occupational safety and health. Existing sources give no AI adoption rate or replacement probability for these two occupations. Calibration, sampling location, operating conditions, regulatory applicability, and control effectiveness must still be verified by trained and authorized people; a model answer cannot directly become an exposure compliance or stop/restart decision. This page also lists the overall 2025—2035 employment growth of 18.6% for the U.S. 19-5000 combined group as employment background only, which cannot be attributed to AI.
entries.question: What judgment boundaries must AI-assisted safety inspection not cross?

entries.answer: When a hazard that could cause serious injury is found in a real setting, first take immediate protection permitted within your scope per unit procedure, record the facts, and escalate to an authorized responsible person. The OSHA hazard prevention and control guidance explains the approach to control and verification in the U.S. context and does not automatically grant readers the right to stop work, test equipment, or restart work in China or other jurisdictions. If authorization is unclear, keep the unknown and contact the site supervisor rather than experimenting on your own.
entries.question: Who decides how to handle a serious hazard once found?
